Templates use complete official argument algorithm and default CLI PackageManager project-first name collision rule; native command names restricted to lowercase alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore for discovery. Other valid Pi filenames still expand in native typed input.
File reads use native ctx.fs, 64 KiB per file / 256 KiB resource budget, 128 templates / 512 directory entries. YAML uses existing js-yaml JSON schema.
Pi project trust dialog/runtime is not transplanted; existing host permissions remain authoritative.

Pi user agentDir context picks first AGENTS.override.md / AGENTS.md / AGENTS.MD / CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.MD via native fs and official project_context text; native workspace instructions are not scanned or duplicated.

Fixed 0.2.1-alpha.1 private roots extension selects cwd.pi plus cwd-to-gitroot ancestor.agents and user directories, with CLI project-first precedence. Bounded native FS directory selection filters native scan inputs and returned candidate paths; actual parsing/get/watch/resource bases remain the same FileSystemSkillProvider. Bundle stops recursion; ignored SKILL does not stop it; Pi root flat files / agents nonroot flat files; dot/node_modules skipped.

Skill and prompt discovery uses upstream ignore@7.0.8 with exact prefixIgnorePattern and .gitignore/.ignore/.fdignore ordering, root-relative paths, directory pruning and negation. Rules inherit within each independent resource root, not from workspace ancestors. Native fs permissions/cancellation and 64 KiB per-rule / 256 KiB aggregate bounds remain authoritative. Native opaque versions detect rule/configuration/explicit-path changes at assembly and invalidate only through the Pi provider registration control; unchanged rules use stat without rescanning skill trees.

Project cwd.pi/settings.json and user agentDir/settings.json skills/prompts use their own base directories, absolute/tilde paths, native resource discovery and upstream minimatch@10.2.6 filter dimensions/order. Explicit project settings precede project auto roots, then explicit user settings, user auto roots, and package resources. Settings globs filter discovered plain entries; package manifest globs are enumerated through bounded native fs.

Existing local directory packages support convention skills/prompts or package.json.pi declarations, package !glob/+exact/-exact filters and empty-array disablement. Project declarations replace the same resolved user package identity; package filters cannot expose manifest-excluded files. No package installation, dependency installation or JS/TS extension execution occurs. Remote sources are diagnosed/skipped, autoload:false deltas skip the affected package identity, and non-Markdown explicit files are rejected by the native provider contract.

guestAdapter.runtime: Extension factories/callbacks only in a separate Node process. No official Pi agent loop, model/account runtime, CLI or SDK executor. Native host owns opt-in module trust, subprocess sandbox, API guards and session/tool loop integration.
adaptations: jiti@2.7.0 loads original TS/JS default factories with fsCache/moduleCache disabled. Original fixed typebox@1.3.27 modules and explicit pure Pi defineTool/typeguard/StringEnum helpers are virtual imports; @sinclair/typebox@0.34.41 remains a separate legacy module alias. Unsupported original runtime exports are absent.

Original validateToolArguments from packages/ai/src/utils/validation.ts is loaded byte-for-byte as a pure helper. It uses fixed typebox/compile Compile, Value.Convert, optional-null normalization and upstream plain JSON Schema coercion. StringEnum retains original Type.Unsafe. No private JSON schema matcher or Pi agent runtime is used. Native host schema/guard checks remain authoritative before guest invocation, so native argument acceptance may be narrower than the original coerced Pi contract.

All factories must succeed before a new registration batch commits. Tools expose original serialized parameters and callback IDs; prepareArguments is exposed as a boolean and rejected by the native host; prepareLoadout descriptions run during native assembly with readonly catalog/getPromptGuidelines metadata, while nonempty hiddenDeclarations explicitly blocks the request. constrainedSampling/renderShell metadata is also rejected because those contracts are not adapted. Active callback registrations and event subscriptions/unsubscriptions use a serial host-acknowledged operation queue. Same-extension replacement and cross-extension first-wins are preserved; a rejected operation rolls back to the acknowledged base and replays later pending changes. Old callback IDs remain valid for already captured native definitions.

Supported events are input, before_agent_start, agent_start, turn_start, agent_end, tool_call, tool_result, session_start and session_shutdown. Unknown event subscriptions fail the factory. Registration order is retained; input transforms form a pipeline and handled stops it; tool_call block stops early and the final input is returned so the native host can reject argument mutations.

Bidirectional complete JSON messages are bounded to 128 MiB through strict wire fragmentation/reassembly; each JSONL frame remains bounded to 2 MiB. Registration descriptions retain a separate budget; 32 modules, 64 active callbacks and 256 pending API calls. Reentrant stdin dispatch and AsyncLocalStorage isolate callback context; cancellation uses per-invocation AbortController. Console output uses stderr. Tool updates retain requestId.

ui.notify/select/confirm/input, exec, executeTool, sendUserMessage and setActiveTools request native host actions; void actions drain their host acknowledgements before callback completion. executeTool is restricted to tool callbacks. setActiveTools updates the callback snapshot immediately for known tools only and waits for preceding registration acknowledgements; nested executeTool also waits for those acknowledgements.

Synchronous getters use only supplied native read-only snapshots; absent required fields and unsupported API properties fail immediately. ctx.model is a limited native id/provider route projection, possibly undefined, without provider credentials or SDK objects. ctx.isProjectTrusted requires an explicit native boolean; otherwise it is unsupported. No fake TUI, account API or separate transcript store is implemented; custom pending messages are native plugin records.

evidence: One Node guest fixture loads the three fixed original official samples and executes hello, protected .env write block and ?quick input transform.

The same fixture verifies ping handled, void ui.notify API acknowledgement drain, a nested hello invoke while that acknowledgement is pending, and failed load without partial registration descriptors.
A focused guest validator fixture verifies plain JSON Schema, original string-to-number coercion, invalid enum rejection and unchanged official hello execution.
verification.limits: The guest fixture does not verify native host permissions, sandbox confinement, native message accounting, UI questions or installed tool-loop integration; those require the host acceptance checks.

steeringAdapter.hostIntegration: Native scoped inbox events track typed next-step identities. Public pre-step mutable messages and native Inbox splice defer remaining steers before native message commit; original id/source kept, notifications/queue unchanged. No loop replacement or custom history.
steeringAdapter.boundary: Native loop claims input and awaits system assembly before pre-step, so cancellation/failure before that hook cannot promise Pi remaining-queue parity.
steeringAdapter.verification: test/installed-pi-steering.test.mjs actual installed two steers, sequential provider requests, preserved message identities and each native user event once

branchesAdapter.hostIntegration: Public native sessionController list/inspect/fork owns observation, completed-prefix seed, journal and parent identity; actual PiBranches UI and authenticated /omaa/api/pi-branches route open native sessions. Optional derived capsule uses native systemPrompt.context and original-session model/API, without another journal or loop.
adaptations: Only idle source sessions and completed turn/end boundaries are forkable; journal head is checked before and after optional summary. Native parent relations form a family of different sessionIds, not an in-place Pi JSONL tree leaf cursor.
Branches share the workspace directory. Switching/forking does not restore file state; parent journals remain unchanged as history sources.

withSummary defaults false in the client. Explicit true summarizes only source events after the selected fork boundary, if material exists. Full original BRANCH_SUMMARY_PROMPT, BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREAMBLE and SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT are extracted verbatim.

Native text parts and tool call/result boundaries are serialized; hidden native reasoning is excluded. Each tool result is capped at2000 characters; newest event chunks are selected up to100000 text characters, with separate read/modified file path lists.

Current session provider/model supplies a no-tools summary request (maxTokens8192, timeout180s), rather than Pi-specific token estimation/retry/provider runtime. Error, abort, max-tokens, empty or over32000-character summary rejects fork; stale source revision also rejects.

Inherited and new summary form a derived context capsule at most60000 characters. Only this bounded data is atomically saved under DSH_HOME/omaa/pi-branch-context by native session hash, and read through native systemPrompt.context including cold startup. Further forks inherit the capsule even with no new summary requested.
Native fork and capsule save are distinct operations: if fork succeeds but capsule save fails, return an explicit error with the created sessionId; do not claim cross-session/file atomic rollback.

extensionHostAdapter.differences: Dynamic registrations use synchronous native scoped registry replacement and rollback. Awaited input and before_agent_start run before native step admission; explicit loadout edits win, otherwise current native active tools supply prompt/catalog. Native custom user/context messages retain Pi metadata. Accepted before_agent_start custom batches use native uiConversation default display with hidden-node handling; journal/model remain unchanged. Native process grouping and collapse remain, not original TUI standalone rows. Complete force uses native journal and leading-system request series, unlike original non-journal request projection. Request-local context/context_with_system transforms and native sendMessage/appendEntry are implemented; custom TUI renderers remain unsupported. Already logged tool arguments stay immutable; result state/details/structuredContent rewriting is limited. Session view covers all supported native messages at one immutable observation, with raw entries separate from current projection; it is not the original Pi JSONL file format, callback actions scoped, dependency installation absent. agent_start/turn_start/agent_end are awaited notifications adapted to native activity/request steps; editable turn_end and agent_before_settle use the boundary adapter. New boundary callbacks run before native idle; legacy notification-only extensions retain idle-reserved runMaintenance. Native retry and original Pi low-level run/pre-settle semantics differ.

beforeAgentStartAdapter.hostIntegration: Native claimed events -> shared steering selection -> awaited input -> nonrecursive templates -> awaited start hook -> native pre-step admission. source.pi.input retains source/template/streaming choices. source.pi.runPrompt retains force presence for cold head cleanup; no second prompt history or queue.
beforeAgentStartAdapter.lifecycle: Once per fresh user run, not per tool/steer/queued streaming follow-up. beforeAgentStartAdapter.limits: Original force is request-only; native DSH logs effective prompt admission. Custom role maps to native user/context with metadata. Default custom-message display is adapted through native uiConversation; request-local full-history transforms are implemented; custom TUI renderers, remaining lifecycle draft APIs and JSONL tree runtime are not present.

adaptations: Pinned upstream convertToLlm maps custom messages to user without checking display. Hidden presentation leaves native journal, model context, message identity and accepted-batch ordering unchanged. No new wakeup inbox or queue.

Default [customType] label and native Markdown use fixed Pi light/dark palette customMessageBg, customMessageText and customMessageLabel. String content is direct; array content extracts text only with newline joins. Images and details are not displayed, matching upstream default rendering.

display:false creates a hidden native view node. Replacement-origin model projections are excluded to avoid duplicate transcript display. Event match uses the function contract supported by rc.2 and alpha.1; alpha-only match tables are not used.
customMessageDisplayAdapter.limits: Accepted before_agent_start batches and sendMessage custom messages. Native DSH process layout may collapse these messages; this is not Pi TUI standalone rows. lifecycleAdapter.hostIntegration: Awaited native step/tool-batch boundaries and native turn pre-idle settlement, retaining the same driver, inbox, dispatcher, prepared provider and journal. Legacy notification-only extensions retain idle-reserved runMaintenance. Cancellation attempts bounded read-only settlement notification before terminating the guest.
adaptations: agent_start has type only; turn_start has turnIndex from zero and dispatch timestamp; agent_end has current-scope actual append-origin messages. Startup/step registrations reassemble the first-request tools and native guard. Pure notification handler errors are reported and later handlers continue.

End-only continuation retains accepted force; fresh human input during end maintenance starts its own before_agent_start and force. Native retry and original Pi low-level prompt/continue scheduling differ.

End messages retain full text/image/toolCall/thinking and original native-only block structures; native attachments supply image bytes. Original Pi replay api/stopReason is retained when present, otherwise native finish reasons are mapped. Native usage is retained with corresponding token fields; no invented SDK costs or guarantee of complete Pi signatures. ctx.sessionManager reads complete supported native messages and current projection from one immutable observation; the 128 MiB transport limit remains explicit.

User-cancel end notification exposes an already-aborted ctx.signal; host forbids exec/executeTool/sendUserMessage/UI questions from resuming work, while notify and read-only APIs remain available. Disposed activity does not start end maintenance. This stop-notification restriction is an OMAA adaptation.

Strict bidirectional wire transport limits complete JSON messages to 128 MiB and individual JSONL frames to 2 MiB, validating sequence, bytes, canonical base64, UTF-8 and completeness without truncation. Registration payloads retain a separate budget.
lifecycleAdapter.limits: Native user turn is not a Pi turn. No arbitrary writable SessionManager, provider-specific signature parity, SDK cost calculation, custom TUI or native partial-tool-result ABI. Unresponsive guest processes cannot guarantee receipt of cancellation notifications.

verification.limits: Native isolated macOS rc.2 with localhost protocol responses; no external model quality, complete Electron, rc.1 or Windows/Linux claim.

historyAdapter.hostIntegration: Public SessionQuery observeSession projection:none captures one immutable cut; public foldSurface plus registered native projections supplies the current ordered message view. Observation is disposed after adaptation. No journal writes or second loop.
adaptations: getEntries supplies all supported native user/assistant/tool-result messages without the previous 100-message/4000-character truncation; getBranch uses the same cut and current projection order.

Native image attachments supply actual bytes; thinking, native-only blocks, actual usage and tool call/result identity are retained. argumentsRaw keeps exact native input alongside the adapted object. Getter clones cannot mutate the native journal.

Tool identity follows native dispatch links, including content-only result replacement chains with stable message IDs. Image conversion is shared only inside one immutable observation; later cuts and other sessions re-read native attachments.
historyAdapter.limits: Supported DSH message view plus durable Pi boundary draft entries, not every Pi JSONL entry or arbitrary writable SessionManager. Context previews use the original pure projection. No invented costs or complete signature parity; callback transport rejects JSON over 128 MiB.

contextAdapter.hostIntegration: Request-local context and context_with_system callbacks before native freeze; original messages and tool declarations remain in the native journal.
contextAdapter.semantics: Serial context handlers receive conversation-only copies; full-system handlers run next. Fixed original Pi system/tool folds restore or render sections. Native request copies are converted before freeze; invalid tool pairs fail before dispatch. Callback changes are transient and never overwrite original journal messages.
contextAdapter.limits: No provider payload/header callbacks or tool execution outside the active native loadout; native attachment admission and 128 MiB guest wire budget remain. Exact rc.2 host module/method fingerprints are required.
contextAdapter.verification: test/installed-pi-context.test.mjs: isolated native rc.2 with localhost synthetic provider; per-request context/system ordering, actual declarations and section rewriting, pruning, callback error isolation, real tool/image pairing, untouched original journal, cold restart, explicit prompt/tool removal, cancellation and invalid pairing rejection.

extensionMessagesAdapter.hostIntegration: Original native inbox for waking steer/followUp; appendPluginRecord for custom state and pending after-step/next-input messages. The original message ID is the durable consumption receipt; default Pi custom-message UI is reused. Awaiting appendEntry refreshes the caller snapshot after host ACK.
extensionMessagesAdapter.limits: Visible message receipts are separate native appends after one authoritative boundary record; recovery appends only missing receipts. Tree navigation and compaction control are provided by sessionControlAdapter.
extensionMessagesAdapter.verification: test/installed-pi-messages.test.mjs: isolated native rc.2, custom state ACK/readback, cold state and next-input queue, single delivery, after-tool append, hidden context, idle display-only and explicit wake.

boundaryAdapter.hostIntegration: One appendPluginRecord batch owns committed drafts. Native message IDs acknowledge custom-message display. Original Pi projection computes serial previews and persistent request context before transient context handlers. Exact rc.2 native turn seam awaits settlement before publishing idle; continuation uses the native inbox with a hidden empty scheduling receipt excluded from model input.
boundaryAdapter.limits: Boundary batches and tree navigation share the effective Pi request projection. Original native history stays intact. Native checkpoints from older sessions supersede absorbed draft contributions; new Pi compaction uses the original Pi preparation and extension callbacks. Unknown plugin records are retained but ignored outside Pi.

sessionControlAdapter.hostIntegration: Original pure tree readers, compaction preparation, branch collection, prompt constants and file tracking. Native appendPluginRecord atomically stores navigation with its summary and label; existing boundary batches store compaction. Request projection uses the selected path, current native system/tools and original attachments. Pi alone replaces basic compaction with branch-aware manual, pressure and one overflow retry. User/project compaction settings, extension hooks and browser controls share this path.
sessionControlAdapter.limits: Native chronological conversation is retained; the Pi tree panel displays the active path. No file rollback, original Pi JSONL import/export, custom TUI, provider signature parity or token-cost claim. Summary tokens are original heuristic estimates. Tool callbacks, context transforms and recursive session operations cannot initiate compaction. Cancellation can terminate an unresponsive extension process before final notification.
